_readme: Triaged red team findings. An entry here means: the attack still succeeds, somebody owns it,
and there is a date by which it will be fixed or re-argued. It does NOT mean the finding is closed.
Every entry needs `owner`, `reason` and `reviewBy`, and `scripts/check-redteam.mjs` refuses to run
without all three. Past `reviewBy` the run FAILS — a caveat is a debt and this file is where the
debts are recorded, not where they are forgiven. Removing an entry whose probe still breaches just
turns the finding back into a NEW_FINDING on the next run, and a probe that starts HOLDING while its
entry is still here fails too, so the record cannot rot in either direction.
To close a finding: fix the code, watch the probe go HELD, then delete the entry.

findings.reason: The dual-signature gate on the payment path counts distinct caller-supplied role strings and verifies no cryptographic material. Accepted for now because (a) both live surfaces currently FAIL CLOSED on receipt minting (LIVE-001), so the path is not issuing receipts, and (b) the fix changes a live authorization gate, which is Sean-gated by the preflight fences. The repo already ships the primitive the fix needs — countersignContract in lib/trustshell/identity/work-contract.ts is a two-party signature over canonical bytes, which is exactly the shape a CFO/CTO co-signature is.

verifyHalChain returns outcome=VERIFIED for a truncated window and signals the truncation only in the separate boolean windowStartUnverifiable, which the human-readable `detail` never mentions. Measured by exhaustive search: no input produces VERIFIED with windowStartUnverifiable=false, so EVERY VERIFIED it can emit is over a window whose start is unexaminable. Accepted short-term because the verifier has no production caller yet — nothing currently reads `outcome` to make a decision — which is exactly why fixing it now is cheap. Deliberately left `unassigned` rather than defaulted to Sean: the fix is a library change, not a Sean-gated one, and a false owner is worse than a visibly missing one.

requireAuditSecret compares against the abandoned default with an exact-string equality after trim, so case variants of the same published constant are accepted. No live surface holds a variant today (LIVE-001 evidence, 2026-08-16). One-line fix: normalise case before comparing.

trustshell.dev's client bundle embeds a LEGACY anon Supabase JWT (project qnnpjhlxljtqyigedwkb, decoded role:anon) confirmed DISABLED by a live PostgREST test — 401 'Legacy API keys are disabled' (2026-08-16). SOURCE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 in DealAppSeo/trustshell@6cfd2d3 lib/supabase.ts (createClient reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY). EXTENDS to the server path: supabaseConfigured() checks key PRESENCE not validity, so submitSuggestion (service_role insert) and the /market + /repid sbSelect reads also 401 IF SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is the legacy service_role JWT (disabled same date) — server env NOT CHECKED. Fails CLOSED (nil confidentiality; anon key is public and dead); cost is availability — any Supabase feature silently broken, same root cause as the 217-day-dead aitrinitysymphony lead form. Fix: redeploy DealAppSeo/trustshell with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=sb_publishable_ AND SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=sb_secret_ (Sean; repo not push-attached here).

repid-engine's PUBLIC score-event path /api/v1/agents-external/:id/score-event has no auth (rate-limit only, no ownership check) — live-confirmed 2026-08-17: an unauthenticated POST reached the scoring handler (HTTP 400 'prompt is required', not 401) against deployed_commit 0b4b391 which matches the reviewed source. The score itself is HAL-computed server-side (a caller cannot write a delta or outcome), so this is an ATTRIBUTION hole, not score fabrication: anyone with an agent UUID (public via /passport + leaderboard) can inject HAL-scored decisions into that agent's history — polluting hallucination stats, dragging it toward the floor with bad answers, or burning HAL/LLM cost (60/IP/min). Impact bounded by HAL (can't fabricate a high score; penalties need a fact-check quorum + penalty-guard trigger + floor). The code's own comment says 'Sprint A8 will harden auth' — a known alpha gap. Fix already exists on the sibling bearer path: requireApiKey(['score_event']) + agent_id ownership check (403 on mismatch); apply it here or restrict the public path to an allowlisted importer. Not applied here — repid-engine is a separate repo, not push-attached, and hardening a live auth path is Sean's. GRIEFING MAGNITUDE MEASURED 2026-08-17 (user-authorized throwaway agent, created+attacked+deleted, 0 rows left): two UNAUTHENTICATED submissions each scored vetoed/hal_score=1/delta -10 (HTTP 200) and were ATTRIBUTED to the victim, but the LIVE current_repid held at 1000 — deltas did not accumulate and never touched the live column (a guard protects it). So the live-score-drain magnitude is ZERO (the 'drain a competitor to the floor' version is REFUTED); the confirmed impact is unauthenticated ATTRIBUTION + history/stats pollution (hallucination_rate, passport/card history) at 60/IP/min + real HAL cost-burn. Severity stays Medium, now measured not speculative. A ledger divergence also surfaced (events store repid_after=990 while current_repid stays 1000, non-accumulating) — MAY be intended earned-vs-applied/floor behaviour, not scored.

The score-event ledger OVERSTATES applied penalties vs the live score, VERIFIED 2026-08-17. Root cause: TWO FLOORS, only one binds. The JS pipeline writes repid_score_events.repid_after/repid_delta_applied from applyToScore()+clampRepidLoud() (clamps to a GLOBAL REPID_MIN), then UPDATEs repid_agents.current_repid; the DB trigger trg_repid_earned_floor (BEFORE UPDATE OF current_repid) re-clamps UP to the PEAK-based tier_lower_bound(peak_repid). When tier_lower_bound(peak) > REPID_MIN (any agent that earned above the bottom tier), a below-floor penalty is absorbed (live moves 0) but the event keeps the full negative delta. Proven behaviourally: writes of 990/950/400 to an agent at earned floor 1000 all clamped to 1000; the grief-test event stored repid_after=990/delta_applied=-10 while live current_repid=1000 (actual movement 0). appliedScoreReconciles() is blind to it — it checks the JS decomposition's internal consistency, not JS-after vs post-trigger live. Severity LOW: audit-accuracy, not exploitable, and it arises from a GOOD control (the earned floor is what makes griefing's live-score magnitude ZERO, REPID-ENG-001). But repid_score_events cannot be summed to reconstruct current_repid, and it feeds REPID-ENG-001's event-log pollution. Fix: clamp the JS applier to the same floor the trigger uses (coalesce(floor_override, tier_lower_bound(peak_repid))) so the event mirrors the actual movement, or store calculated AND true-applied with distinct labels. Left unassigned: the fix is a repid-engine code change (separate repo, not push-attached), not a Sean-gated infra action.

CORRECTS CLAUDE.md's OPEN item, which says 0xdf6b8215 has 'balance 0, nonce 0' — that is MAINNET; on the operative testnet chain both are active+funded, so the exposure is real, not inert. MITIGANTS (held): reputation-write authority is ROTATED to 0xb2426888 (not leaked), so reputation writes aren't forgeable via these keys; and value at risk is testnet ETH only (mainnet inert). Impact: identity-anchor control on the operative chain — anyone with repo history holds the funded key that minted the identities. Escalates to High/Critical if this moves to mainnet unrotated. FIX: rotate the keys per docs/KEY-ROTATION.md. BLOCKED_FOR_SEAN — CLAUDE.md is explicit no agent session runs the rotation (needs the live key in a transcripted context, which is how it leaked). NOT CHECKED: whether the current EIP-712 attestation signer HYPERDAG_ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEY is the rotated key or still 0xf6eE (off-chain, env-only).
